core.text: MetaJudge is designed to evaluate the consistency between model-generated critiques and human expert checklists. Given an original evaluation list (model-generated) and a reference evaluation list (human checklist), MetaJudge determines the extent to which each item in the original list achieves the intended purpose/improvement goal of each item in the reference list. See Figure 9 for the MetaJudge prompt used for strict one-to-one semantic matching and scoring.
Appendix D Training and Evaluation Details

We train the Generative Reward Model (GenRM) using the GRPO algorithm with the following key hyperparameters: learning rate of 2×10−62\times 10^{-6}, batch size of 256, mini-batch size of 128. We sample n=8n=8 responses per prompt with a maximum generation length of 12K tokens and maximum prompt length of 8K tokens. The positive and negative clip ratios are both set to 2×10−42\times 10^{-4}. The model is trained for 2 epochs in total. The training prompt for GenRM is shown in Figure 13.

For downstream policy alignment, we also employ the GRPO algorithm with the following hyperparameters: learning rate of 2×10−62\times 10^{-6}, batch size of 512, mini-batch size of 128. We sample n=8n=8 responses per prompt with a maximum generation length of 12K tokens and maximum prompt length of 8K tokens. The positive and negative clip ratios are set to 2×10−42\times 10^{-4}. The policy model is trained for 90 steps using the trained GenRM as the reward signal.
